summary:
t9-dials-2 is fixed in the kit (src/js/70-dial.js, function stepFrom inside addDial; the style sheet is unchanged). Started 06:28, last test 06:51, page builds, smoke test exit 0.

What the user gets: on Trap thickness, Surface threshold and Fly speed the arrows now come back to round values after touching the low limit. Trap thickness from 0.01: down 0.005, 0.0005, 0.0005, then up 0.005, 0.01, 0.015 (before: 0.0055, 0.0105, 0.0155). Surface threshold: 0.05, 0.02, then up 0.05, 0.1, 0.15 (before 0.07, 0.12, 0.17). Fly speed: 0.01, 0.001, then up 0.01, 0.02, 0.03 (before 0.011, 0.021, 0.031).

The rule, as the tester suggested, in two parts, both acting only at a typed limit that is no round value: (1) leaving such a limit, the first step lands on the next round value; (2) a step that would pass such a limit stops on the last round value before it, and only from there goes to the limit (this matters for ten steps at once with Shift or Page keys). "Round values" are the usual slider's positions carried on past its ends; for every dial of the page these are the whole multiples of the step (measured).

One part of the tester's wording I deliberately did not follow: a typed value between the round ones (2.37 on Power n, 0.0125 on Trap thickness) still keeps its odd part when stepped. The kit has done that since round 1 (one of its own 71 checks says "Fine steps never snap to a grid") and the first check recorded "from 2.37 give 2.47, 3.47, 2.47, 2.37" as a pass, which had to stay. Once such a value meets the limit, the arrows are back on round values. The tester's stated "expected" is met. Still as before: the last press down goes from 0.005 to 0.0005 in one step (the tester named and allowed it).

Every dial gains: walked all 51 number boxes at both ends before and after. Usual ranges: 48 the same, 3 changed (the three named). Extreme ranges: 45 the same, 6 changed (the same three plus Mosaic cell size, Turning-out sphere radius, Ray step share, each with a low limit of 0.005 or 0.002 off its grid). The boxes that changed are exactly those with a limit off their grid.

What did not change (recorded on dist/v9m.html before touching the source, repeated after): the first check's driver gives 144 result lines on both pages, identical character for character (dials 84 pass 0 fail, resets 34 pass 2 fail as on every version since 6, extreme 24 pass 0 fail), and the same list of 51 boxes; the kit's own 71 checks pass before and after; round 7's 13 extra checks pass.

Measured: all of the above in headless Chrome, with real mouse, keys and finger taps through the DevTools protocol for the tester's grid.py, my real.py and phone.py and the first check's driver; scripted presses for the 51-box walk and the kit checks. Only reasoned: the second tester's other scripts (new9.py, recheck.py) were not run again; the sweep button, typing, the slider and the whole-number toggle do not pass through the changed lines. Notes: notes/r10-dial.md.
files_changed: src/css/70-dial.css: NOT changed (same bytes as base9m/css/70-dial.css)

The defect's own words (Trap thickness from 0.05, down ten times, then up) plus Shift-click, a held arrow and the keys in the box, real input: out/r10/dial/real-after.log 13 pass 0 fail on my page, real-before.log 6 pass 7 fail on v9m. Finger taps at 375 x 812: out/r10/dial/phone-after.log 4 pass 0 fail. All 51 boxes at both ends, usual and extreme ranges: out/r10/dial/ends-diff.log (usual 48 same, 3 changed; extreme 45 same, 6 changed; all changes are to round values). Unchanged: first check's driver 144 of 144 result lines identical between v9m and my page (out/r10/dial/t6-compare.log, t6-on-v9m.log, t6-on-r10.log); kit page 71 of 71 before and after (kit-tests-before.log, kit-tests-after.log); 14 new kit checks pass (kit-extra.log); round 7's 13 pass (kit-extra-r7.log); smoke test tools/smoke-v9m.json on dist/r10-dial.html exit 0, 52 steps, no console errors (out/r10/dial/smoke.log). Pictures looked at: out/r10/dial/after-thick-low.png (0.0005 at the limit), after-thick-up.png (one press up: 0.005, thumb on the slider's lowest position), before-thick-up.png (0.0055), after-phone-thick-up.png (phone, 0.005, clean row).

names_added: stepFrom: same name and arguments, new body for the fine step; no id, class, label, tooltip, CSS property or spec option added or changed
needs_from_others: src/body.html closing text: I found no sentence about the dial arrows there (searched base9m/body.html for arrow, ±, step, whole number), so nothing needs rewording because of this change.

Not a filed defect, for the owner of src/js/80-ui.js: with Extreme ranges on, the slider of Surface threshold starts at 0.02 and moves by 0.05 (qdetail, xmin: 0.02), so the slider itself gives 0.07, 0.12. Changing xmin to 0.05 would keep that slider on round values. The arrows now return to 0.05, 0.1 from the limit there regardless.
Optional, for whoever owns tests/dial.html: it could take the 14 checks of out/r10/dial/kit-extra.js (and round 7's 13 from out/r7/dial/kit-extra.js).
Person joining the files: take src/js/70-dial.js whole; src/css/70-dial.css has no change.
risks: A typed value between the round ones still keeps its odd part when stepped (typed 0.0125 on Trap thickness goes 0.0175 up, 0.0075 and 0.0025 down) until it meets the limit. This is on purpose (the kit's own check 'Fine steps never snap to a grid' and the first check's 2.37 line), but a tester reading the suggested fix literally may expect a typed value to snap as well.
The arrow tooltips still say 'Up by 0.005' and 'Down by 0.005'; the single step that leaves an odd limit is shorter than that (0.0005 to 0.005). Words left alone, since labels were not to change.

With Shift (ten steps) a press that would pass an odd limit now stops on the last round value first (Trap thickness 0.03: 0.005, then 0.0005; before 0.0005 at once). One more press is needed to reach the very limit. This follows the tester's suggestion and affects only the 3 dials (6 with extreme ranges) whose limit is off the grid.

Only headless Chrome on this machine was used. The second tester's new9.py and recheck.py were not rerun on my page; I reasoned from the changed code paths and my own runs that their results hold, apart from the two lines of part 'thick' that describe this fault.

The first check's driver still shows its 2 old FAIL lines in 'resets' (Julia and Kleinian lists), on the base page and on mine alike; the first tester explained them as their table being too strict. They are not a dial matter.
